name: Grafton Milk Biscuits
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: one-third of a teaspoonful of soda
ingredients.originalText: one-third of a teaspoonful of soda

instructions.text: Boil and mash two white potatoes
Add two teaspoonfuls of brown sugar
Pour boiling water over these, enough to soften them
When tepid, add one small teacupful of yeast
When light, warm three ounces of butter in one pint of milk with a little salt and one-third of a teaspoonful of soda
Add flour enough to make stiff sponge
When risen, work it on the board
Put it back in the tray to rise again
When risen, roll into cakes and let them stand half an hour

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Boil and mash two white potatoes
2. Add two teaspoonfuls of brown sugar
3. Pour boiling water over these, enough to soften them
4. When tepid, add one small teacupful of yeast
5. When light, warm three ounces of butter in one pint of milk with a little salt and one-third of a teaspoonful of soda
6. Add flour enough to make stiff sponge
7. When risen, work it on the board
8. Put it back in the tray to rise again
9. When risen, roll into cakes and let them stand half an hour
10. Bake in a quick oven
